scope: Primary sources checked for the physics-focused presentation; no claim that off-sector extension diagnostics are algorithmically novel.

references.title: Solving the Quantum Many-Body Problem with Artificial Neural Networks
references.supports: Finite-size VMC at the critical TFI point and gapless Heisenberg models; energy accuracy can be high. This is a counterexample to categorical gapless VMC failure, not a guarantee for our bosonic models.

references.title: Specialising neural-network quantum states for the Bose Hubbard model
references.authors: M. Y. Pei and S. R. Clark
references.supports: Fixed-number occupation basis, particle-conserving Metropolis sampling, energy/variance and correlator diagnostics for NQS-VMC. Equations10–12 and surrounding text explicitly describe restricting sampled configurations to N.

references.title: Autoregressive Neural Quantum States with Quantum Number Symmetries
references.authors: A. Malyshev, J. M. Arrazola and A. I. Lvovsky
references.supports: Explicit quantum-number-constrained autoregressive sampling; a different established route to symmetry enforcement, not a proposed architecture change here.

references.title: Monte Carlo study of the two-dimensional Bose-Hubbard model
references.supports: Square-lattice unit-filling SF–MI transition, U/2 convention, thermodynamic critical coupling and gap behavior; does not imply our small clusters or width4cylinders are already gapless.

derived_here: Finite-sector spectral decomposition gives E-E0>=Delta_N*(1-F_abs^2) for nondegenerate ground state.
Fixed-N data are unchanged by arbitrary additive h(N) with h(N0)=0 in raw log amplitude.
Full-space overlap with a zero-embedded canonical target equals sqrt(Pfull(N0))*canonicaloverlap.
